17:1.sourceText: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάνην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν.
17:1.targetText: And after six days Jesus takes Peter, and James, and his brother John, and brings them up to a high mountain by themselves,

groups.note: The actual κατ’ ἰδίαν phrase supplies the complete by themselves solitude expression, without inventing a separately written reflexive pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus, Peter or his brother John.

17:2.sourceText: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.
17:2.targetText: and He was transfigured before them, and His face shone as the sun, and His garments became white as the light,

groups.note: The Greek singular became verb agrees with its neuter plural garments subject. The source form is kept rather than changed to an English-shaped plural.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with His face and His garments.

17:3.sourceText: καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἡλείας συνλαλοῦντες μετ’ αὐτοῦ.
17:3.targetText: and behold, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking together with Him.

groups.note: The actual singular appearing verb is used before the coordinated Moses and Elijah subjects; the source singular is preserved.

17:4.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἡλείᾳ μίαν.
17:4.targetText: And Peter answering said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good to us to be here; if You will, we may make three shelters here: one for You, and one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”

groups.note: The actual accusative ἡμᾶς is the subject of to be in the good-to-be construction; English renders its participant relation as to us rather than supplying a separate Greek preposition.
The actual θέλω verb expresses willing or wishing, not a future auxiliary.

N1904 has the first-person singular future ποιήσω, I will make, whereas LSV follows we may make. Only the shared making predicate and its English modal expression are paired; the differing plural we subject is explained separately.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Peter is not separately expressed in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows the plural we wording for making the shelters; pinned N1904 has the first-person singular ποιήσω, not a first-person plural subject.

17:5.sourceText: ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος, ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ Υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.
17:5.targetText: While he is yet speaking, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud, saying, “This is My Son, the Beloved, in whom I delighted; hear Him.”

groups.note: The present speaking participle in the genitive-absolute construction supplies While ... is ... speaking; the temporal relation belongs to this actual participial clause, not an invented Greek while word or be verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with My Son.

17:6.sourceText: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.
17:6.targetText: And the disciples having heard, fell on their face, and were exceedingly afraid,

17:7.sourceText: καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.
17:7.targetText: and Jesus having come near, touched them, and said, “Rise, do not be afraid,”

groups.note: The Greek finite approached verb προσῆλθεν is rendered having come near; its actual finite form is retained.
The Greek touching participle ἁψάμενος is rendered as the finite touched predicate; the same touching head is retained.

The Greek and connecting approaching with the touching/saying continuation is rendered before said as English recasts the first finite verb as a participle and the touching participle as a finite predicate.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus and the connectives between approaching/touching and rising/not fearing are not separately expressed in the corresponding English clauses.

17:8.sourceText: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.
17:8.targetText: and having lifted up their eyes, they saw no one, except Jesus only.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their eyes.
The Greek intensive αὐτόν accompanying Jesus is not separately expressed beyond the English Jesus only description.

17:9.sourceText: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.
17:9.targetText: And as they are coming down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, “Say to no one the vision, until the Son of Man may rise out of the dead.”

groups.note: The actual descending participle in the genitive-absolute construction supplies as ... are coming down; the temporal relation is carried by that clause rather than a separately written Greek as or be verb.
The actual passive-form ἐγερθῇ is rendered may rise; the source grammatical voice remains visible rather than changed to match the English expression.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.

17:10.sourceText: Καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἡλείαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;
17:10.targetText: And His disciples questioned Him, saying, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with His disciples.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly writes the disciples possessor His; pinned N1904 has the disciples without a separate possessive pronoun.

17:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἡλείας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·
17:11.targetText: And Jesus answering said to them, “Elijah does indeed come first, and will restore all things,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article supplies the understood answerer; English follows the named Jesus introduction rather than separately rendering that article.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV names Jesus; pinned N1904 has the article-led answering subject without a written Jesus name in this verse.
LSV explicitly states the saying recipients; pinned N1904 has said without a separate recipient pronoun here.
LSV includes first with Elijah coming; pinned N1904 has Elijah indeed comes without a separate first modifier in this verse.

17:12.sourceText: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἡλείας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν, ἀλλ’ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν.
17:12.targetText: and I say to you, Elijah already came, and they did not know him, but did with him whatever they would, so also the Son of Man is about to suffer by them.”

groups.note: The actual θέλω verb supplies they would in the sense of what they wanted, not an independent future auxiliary.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek quotation connector ὅτι is not separately expressed before the English Elijah declaration.

17:13.sourceText: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάνου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.
17:13.targetText: Then the disciples understood that He spoke to them concerning John the Immerser.

17:14.sourceText: Καὶ ἐλθόντων πρὸς τὸν ὄχλον προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ ἄνθρωπος γονυπετῶν αὐτὸν
17:14.targetText: And when they came to the multitude, there came to Him a man, kneeling down to Him,

groups.note: The actual genitive-absolute coming participle supplies the temporal when they came clause. English makes its implicit plural subject explicit without introducing a different original pronoun.
The actual accusative αὐτόν is governed by the kneeling expression, rendered to Him. The original case remains accusative rather than an invented dative.

17:15.sourceText: καὶ λέγων Κύριε, ἐλέησόν μου τὸν υἱόν, ὅτι σεληνιάζεται καὶ κακῶς ἔχει· πολλάκις γὰρ πίπτει εἰς τὸ πῦρ καὶ πολλάκις εἰς τὸ ὕδωρ.
17:15.targetText: and saying, “Lord, deal kindly with my son, for he is [a] lunatic, and suffers miserably, for he often falls into the fire, and often into the water,

groups.note: The actual verb σεληνιάζεται is rendered he is [a] lunatic, the edition’s historical wording. This aligns the printed verbal description without adding a Greek be verb.
The actual κακῶς ἔχει expression describes being badly afflicted, rendered suffers miserably; the state verb is retained with its adverb rather than treated as a separate suffering lemma.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with my son.

17:16.sourceText: καὶ προσήνεγκα αὐτὸν τοῖς μαθηταῖς σου, καὶ οὐκ ἠδυνήθησαν αὐτὸν θεραπεῦσαι.
17:16.targetText: and I brought him near to Your disciples, and they were not able to heal him.”

17:17.sourceText: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν Ὦ γενεὰ ἄπιστος καὶ διεστραμμένη, ἕως πότε μεθ’ ὑμῶν ἔσομαι; ἕως πότε ἀνέξομαι ὑμῶν; φέρετέ μοι αὐτὸν ὧδε.
17:17.targetText: And Jesus answering said, “O generation, unsteadfast and perverse, until when will I be with you? Until when will I bear you? Bring him to Me here”;

groups.note: The actual faithless/unbelieving adjective ἄπιστος is rendered unsteadfast in this translation; its written lemma is retained rather than replaced with an invented stability verb.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article before Jesus is not separately expressed in English.

17:18.sourceText: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ τὸ δαιμόνιον, καὶ ἐθεραπεύθη ὁ παῖς ἀπὸ τῆς ὥρας ἐκείνης.
17:18.targetText: and Jesus rebuked him, and the demon went out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus or that hour.

17:19.sourceText: Τότε προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ τῷ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἰδίαν εἶπον Διὰ τί ἡμεῖς οὐκ ἠδυνήθημεν ἐκβαλεῖν αὐτό;
17:19.targetText: Then the disciples having come to Jesus by Himself, said, “Why were we not able to cast him out?”

groups.note: The actual κατ’ ἰδίαν solitude phrase supplies by Himself in the disciples’ private approach to Jesus; no separately written third-person reflexive pronoun is invented.
The original neuter demon pronoun αὐτό is rendered English him for that same demon being cast out. The written source pronoun remains neuter.

17:20.sourceText: ὁ δὲ λέγει αὐτοῖς Διὰ τὴν ὀλιγοπιστίαν ὑμῶν· ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐρεῖτε τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ Μετάβα ἔνθεν ἐκεῖ, καὶ μεταβήσεται, καὶ οὐδὲν ἀδυνατήσει ὑμῖν.
17:20.targetText: And Jesus said to them, “Through your want of faith; for truly I say to you, if you may have faith as a grain of mustard, you will say to this mountain, Move from here to there, and it will move, and nothing will be impossible to you,

groups.note: The Greek present λέγει is rendered past said; the actual saying head and its source present tense are retained.
The actual little-faith noun ὀλιγοπιστία is rendered want of faith; this phrase remains with that one written noun rather than an invented separate faith head.
The actual inability verb ἀδυνατέω supplies will be impossible; the English be-impossible expression is verbal, not an added independent Greek be verb.

The Greek article is not separately expressed with your want-of-faith expression.

17:22.sourceText: Συστρεφομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Μέλλει ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου παραδίδοσθαι εἰς χεῖρας ἀνθρώπων,
17:22.targetText: And while they are living in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men,

17:23.sourceText: καὶ ἀποκτενοῦσιν αὐτόν, καὶ τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγερθήσεται. καὶ ἐλυπήθησαν σφόδρα.
17:23.targetText: and they will kill Him, and the third day He will rise,” and they were exceedingly sorry.

groups.note: The actual future passive raising form ἐγερθήσεται is rendered He will rise. Its source grammatical voice remains visible.

17:24.sourceText: Ἐλθόντων δὲ αὐτῶν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ προσῆλθον οἱ τὰ δίδραχμα λαμβάνοντες τῷ Πέτρῳ καὶ εἶπαν Ὁ διδάσκαλος ὑμῶν οὐ τελεῖ δίδραχμα;
17:24.targetText: And they having come to Capernaum, those receiving the didrachmas came near to Peter and said, “Your teacher—does He not pay the didrachmas?” He says, “Yes.”

groups.note: Pinned Greek places Peter’s He says, Yes response at 17:25; this LSV edition prints it at the end of 17:24. The actual original reference is retained.

17:25.sourceText: λέγει Ναί. καὶ ἐλθόντα εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν προέφθασεν αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων Τί σοι δοκεῖ, Σίμων; οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς ἀπὸ τίνων λαμβάνουσιν τέλη ἢ κῆνσον; ἀπὸ τῶν υἱῶν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀπὸ τῶν ἀλλοτρίων;
17:25.targetText: And when he came into the house, Jesus anticipated him, saying, “What do you think, Simon? The kings of the earth—from whom do they receive custom or poll-tax? From their sons or from the strangers?”

groups.note: The actual coming participle is an accusative participant construction with Jesus anticipating him, recast as when he came. Its temporal relation and English he are supplied by that actual participial participant, not a new original pronoun.
The actual second-person dative σοι marks the experiencer of δοκεῖ, what seems to you, recast as the English subject you in what do you think. Its source dative remains visible.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with Jesus or their sons.

sourceMoved.reason: The written response He says, Yes appears at the end of LSV 17:24; its groups there preserve the actual Greek 17:25 identities.

17:27.sourceText: ἵνα δὲ μὴ σκανδαλίσωμεν αὐτούς, πορευθεὶς εἰς θάλασσαν βάλε ἄγκιστρον καὶ τὸν ἀναβάντα πρῶτον ἰχθὺν ἆρον, καὶ ἀνοίξας τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εὑρήσεις στατῆρα· ἐκεῖνον λαβὼν δὸς αὐτοῖς ἀντὶ ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ.
17:27.targetText: but that we may not cause them to stumble, having gone to the sea, cast a hook, and the fish that has come up first take up, and having opened its mouth, you will find a stater, that having taken, give to them for Me and you.”
